answer:
The vapour pressure of water at 180 °C from the Antoine equation is about **9.97 bar (7480 mmHg, 0.997 MPa)**.

I used the high-temperature constants for water, valid from 99 to 374 °C, with P in mmHg and T in °C:
log10 P = 8.14019 − 1810.94 / (244.485 + T)
At T = 180 °C this gives P = 7481 mmHg = 9.97 bar.

**Check against an independent value:** CoolProp, which uses the IAPWS reference equation for water, gives 10.03 bar at 453.15 K. The Antoine result is about 0.5 % low.

**Which constants you use matters a lot at this temperature:**

| Antoine constant set | Result | Error vs 10.03 bar |
|---|---|---|
| 99–374 °C set (above) | 9.97 bar | −0.5 % |
| Common 1–100 °C set (A = 8.07131, B = 1730.63, C = 233.426), used outside its range | 10.24 bar | +2 % |
| NIST WebBook set for 379–573 K (A = 3.55959, B = 643.748, C = −198.043; bar, K), within its stated range | 10.87 bar | +8 % |

I computed all these numbers with a single Python one-liner and created no files. If you need better accuracy than about 1 %, use the steam-table / IAPWS value of 10.03 bar rather than any Antoine fit.
